catalog.name: HydroRIVERS
catalog.description: HydroRIVERS is a comprehensive global river network dataset containing 8.5 million individual river reaches with a total length of 35.9 million km. It includes all rivers with a catchment area of at least 10 km² or an average flow of at least 0.1 m³/sec. Extracted from the HydroSHEDS database at 15 arc-second resolution, each river segment contains key attributes including length, distance from headwaters and ocean outlets, river order, and estimated long-term average discharge. All reaches are co-registered with the HydroBASINS database through shared IDs, making it ideal for hydrological modeling and water resource management.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: HydroRIVERS dataset by Lehner, B., Grill G. (2013). Global river hydrography and network routing: baseline data and new approaches to study the world's large river systems. Hydrological Processes, 27(15): 2171–2186. Data distributed by McGill University and World Wildlife Fund.

info.content: Available for non-commercial use. For commercial use, please contact the HydroSHEDS team.

info.name: Background
info.content: HydroRIVERS provides detailed river network information for Africa, including all major river systems like the Nile, Congo, Niger, and Zambezi rivers. Each river segment contains hydrological attributes for water resource assessment.

info.name: Data Coverage
info.content: Complete coverage of African continent river networks with minimum catchment area of 10 km² or flow of 0.1 m³/sec.

info.name: Applications
info.content: Supports hydrological modeling, water resource management, flood risk assessment, and environmental studies across Africa.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: HydroRIVERS by Lehner & Grill (2013), McGill University and World Wildlife Fund.

info.name: Background
info.content: Arctic river networks including rivers in northern Canada, Alaska, and northern Russia. These systems are crucial for understanding climate change impacts on Arctic hydrology.

info.name: Applications
info.content: Climate change research, Arctic hydrology, and permafrost-river interactions.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: HydroRIVERS by Lehner & Grill (2013), McGill University and World Wildlife Fund.

info.name: Background
info.content: Comprehensive river networks for Asia including major systems like the Ganges, Brahmaputra, Mekong, Yangtze, and Yellow rivers. Critical for water security in the world's most populous region.

info.name: Applications
info.content: Transboundary water management, monsoon hydrology, water security assessment, and regional water resource planning.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: HydroRIVERS by Lehner & Grill (2013), McGill University and World Wildlife Fund.
